correctness.rationale: The fixed-node conditional-bridge covariance decomposes into independent intervals and gives exactly the cubic-gap loss. The explicit continuous dual potential satisfies the global polynomial inequality: on opposite halves its nonnegative deficit factors (d−1/2)^2(d+1); on a single half the derivative and endpoint bound are nonnegative. Integrating the dual against two uniform marginals gives exact bound E[V]>=1/64. Equality forces exactly half-period separation a.s., uniquely determining the joint law because the first marginal is atomless. Direct exact-fraction finite tests (22,248 checks) passed and independently compare Gram regression with conditional-bridge reduction; they supplement, not replace, the global proof. Boundary cases, collisions and singular couplings are included.

value.rationale: Calibration to individually uniform sites is a natural constraint in randomized numerical integration. This theorem optimizes all joint dependence, proves a sharp unique solution with a concrete pointwise dual certificate, and quantifies a 37.5% expected posterior variance improvement over independence; central reflection has strictly worse risk than iid. That distinction is structural and nontrivial even though the optimal shifted-grid construction itself is familiar. Scope and the unconstrained deterministic comparison are explicitly restricted.
